transcript: I am not a dancer, but I couldn't help myself. I just had to join the ceilidh. Hello from Baltimore. We are here for ceilidh, a new Scottish musical, and I'm so excited. Directed by Sam Pinkleton. Don't really know a lot about it except that there's dancing, so really in I love Scotland. I will never stop talking about the Edinburgh Fringe. One of the most joyful traditions in Scotland is a ceilidh which is basically a social gathering with music and dances and storytelling. It's about connection and community. This ceilidh though, is a new musical playing at the M&T Bank Exchange Theatre in Baltimore. It's a story of family and legacy and love, and it's about the callers of a ceilidh the people who lead you in the dances so during the show. They actually encourage the audience to join in. I love this show so much The show is so fun, but also very very moving. It very much had come from away or curious case of Benjamin Button vibes. I am so happy there is so much dancing. Like, you don't have to dance, but they encourage people to come up. They do these group dances and it's just a blast. The music is really, really beautiful, and the way that Sam Pinkleton directed this. we just got snacks so can't complain. I'm so excited for act two excited to get up and dance. I love getting to dance with people, but I also Loved watching people dance. It's like you're watching a community form right in front of your eyes. The cast is so good and engaging and just, like, brings everyone together. Makes you feel safe and comfortable to participate. I also got to see Courtney Bassett, who I just adore. She brought so, so much light and joy and talent to this production. I am so happy we made the trip. This is a show that we all need right now. It's only running for a few more days in Baltimore, but hopefully I get to see it again. I am so happy It has to come to New York. It's the best time. Incredible cast, incredible story. I love ceilidh.
